newsitem.title: FRANCE: French activists block gene-modified maize.
newsitem.headline: French activists block gene-modified maize.

text.p: Greenpeace activists on Friday blockaded a warehouse in a western French port where they said several tonnes of gene-modified U.S. maize is stored, witnesses said.

The environmentalists chained themselves to the gates of the warehouse in Montoir, near Saint-Nazaire. They said they were protesting that France had not banned imports of the maize though it had banned production in France.

The grain had been seized as the French government pondered how to deal with gene-modified maize. Customs oficers said it had now been released since France had decided to allow the import of the grain, and most of it had left the warehouse.

Days after it allowed imports of the gene-modified maize, subject to labelling conditions, the French government on Wednesday banned sowings of the maize for at least a year, saying it wanted to move step by step on a complex issue.
Environmentalists and some consumer groups have campaigned against the maize, designed to withstand the borer pest, saying it may cause damage to health.
